title: Frontend: once(fn)
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind once(fn). This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(values). A callback returns its supplied number and increments a call count. Wrap it with once, call the wrapper for each value, and return {outputs,calls}. Cache falsey and zero results; no calls means calls=0.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Store a hasResult flag separately from the cached value so undefined, zero, and false can still be valid results.
alternativeApproaches: Create an async once variant and choose whether rejected work is cached or retried.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Returns undefined; returns zero; throws then succeeds.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
